title: Why spec-driven development
intro: Four minutes on why 'make it green and big' doesn't scale — and what replaces it.

steps.title: Vibe coding: fast, and disposable
steps.body:
The loop: vague prompt → eyeball the result → correct by chatting. *"Make it green and big"* → overshoots → *"Not so big!!!"* → finally right.

Fine for a button. But **nothing is captured** — the dialogue that shaped the code is thrown away, and what remains is disposable code, technical debt, and drift.

steps.title: The spec is the brain
steps.body:
SDD's answer is a **maintained specification** — a permanent, version-controlled artifact that decouples the **what & why** (spec) from the **how** (implementation).

> [!key] The agent is the muscle; the spec is the brain. Your job becomes converting intentions into clear specifications.

Like a compiler turning source into machine code, SDD turns `spec.md` into source code — except the 'source' is now **human-readable intent** stakeholders can read.

points.label: Small edits
points.note: A few sentences of spec → hundreds of lines of code. Steer a fast agent with low cognitive overhead.

points.label: No decay
points.note: Chat context fills up and the agent degrades. Specs persist across sessions AND across agents — every run re-anchors.

points.label: Fidelity
points.note: The spec forces problem, success criteria, constraints, flows BEFORE code exists — output matches intent.

steps.title: Why it needs an agent, not a chatbot
steps.body:
A **chatbot** only talks about code you paste in — its context balloons and it can't act. An **agent** plans, reasons, and reaches your codebase and tools (files, DB, terminal).

In SDD you are the **senior architect** with the blueprints; the agent is a highly capable pair programmer. The result isn't just functional software — it's software aligned with your long-term goals.

recap:
**Vibe coding throws intent away; SDD makes it a permanent artifact.**

- Spec = the brain (what & why); agent = the muscle (how).
- Benefits: small edits → large changes; no context decay; intent fidelity.
- The spec is a universal contract — humans ↔ humans, humans ↔ agent.
- Requires a tool-using agent, not a paste-code-into-chat bot.
